note: Forge-neutral description of how a CI system should run the DESIGN_SPEC section 4 gates. It declares what the environment must provide, because a pipeline cannot provision something the gate spec does not ask for. It does not schedule anything and blocks no pull request; scripts/ci_pipeline.py is what a pipeline would invoke.

forge_target.caveat: rd-intelligence has no git remote, so this configuration cannot execute here. It is written against the conventional target and is auditable as a declaration, not as a running pipeline.

0.meaning: all section 4 gates implemented, required execution satisfied, all passed

2.meaning: a gate reported REGRESSION: a content difference was observed

3.meaning: a gate could not execute: missing environment, unrunnable gate, or a discovery failure. Fail-closed, and never reported as a regression.

4.meaning: UNKNOWN or NOT_IMPLEMENTED: no content conclusion was formed. Needs a human; must not be auto-promoted.

pipeline_preconditions.note: A failure here is the pipeline layer's own, and is INFRASTRUCTURE. It is distinct from any gate verdict and must never be recorded as a regression.

environment_requirements.provided_by: runner with a GPU and a matching driver, plus a built RenderDoc pymodule and a capture
environment_requirements.note: A hosted runner without a GPU cannot satisfy this. The correct outcome is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, not a pass and not a regression. The capture is NOT in version control: tests/workload/corpus is gitignored and zero .rdc files are tracked, so a fresh clone cannot run this gate until the corpus is supplied out of band. The correct outcome of a missing capture is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE.

It spawns workers that replay, so it needs the same environment even though it runs no unittest suite. The capture is NOT in version control: tests/workload/corpus is gitignored and zero .rdc files are tracked, so a fresh clone cannot run this gate until the corpus is supplied out of band. The correct outcome of a missing capture is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE.

environment_requirements.provided_by: a second checkout next to this repository
environment_requirements.note: Without it the fork audit cannot run and reports INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE. The pipeline must not substitute a copy of the F1 to F4 logic to make this pass.

PROCESS_ONLY. A process requirement with no executable check. It is declared here so every gate in the gate spec has a stated environment, and it keeps the overall result off PASS. No runner capability can satisfy it, and none is invented.

artifacts.note: Both are machine readable. The report has to carry gate-level state, executed, required_execution, command, result and the overall state, so that a reader can tell what ran from what was merely reported.

release_blocking.note: Release blocking is not authorized. Until it is, an exit 4 is a legitimate resting state and the overall result stays NEEDS_REVIEW because section 4 gate 4 has no executable check.

schema_history.rdebug-ci-pipeline/4: Per-gate rows carry missing_prerequisites, discovery_anomaly and spec_gate as fields rather than only as prose inside detail, and carry a lint sub-record when the gate declares a lint precondition. Contract 6.1 declared the first two; they were previously unreadable by a machine.

capability_declaration.note: DESIGN_SPEC 4.2.1. These are execution prerequisites, not semantic checks. Resolved by scripts/pipeline_readiness.py, which observes and reports; it never installs, downloads or clones.

corpus.note: Corpus is supplied externally and is not version controlled. presence is an observation of this machine; required/source/tracked/provenance_required are declarations. Absence is INFRASTRUCTURE_FAILURE, never REGRESSION and never PASS.
